A first stop before [Classic Synths Compared](synth-compare.qmd). Short sections, one idea each. Click a heading to fold or open it.

::: {.ik-do}
**What you'll do**

1. Read what Vital is: a free software synth.
2. Learn its sound, one idea at a time.
3. Take the guided tour, one **▶ Hear step** at a time: a first sound, shaping it, a bass, a pad and a lead.
4. Install the real Vital (free) and copy your patch across, setting by setting.
5. Check yourself with a short quiz.
:::

## What it is

- **Vital** is a *software synthesizer*: a program, not a box with keys. It runs inside a music program (a DAW) as a *plug-in*.
- Its source code calls it "a spectral warping wavetable synthesizer" (Vital README, github.com/mtytel/vital). It is by **Matt Tytel**, named in that README; first released in 2020 (unverified).
- There is a **free version**: the README speaks of "the free version of Vital", and vital.audio lists *Basic* with 75 presets and 25 wavetables, beside paid tiers *Plus* and *Pro*.
- Its source code is open, under the GPLv3 licence (README).

## Its sound

- Each oscillator plays a **wavetable**: a row of single-cycle waves. The **Wave frame** knob picks a place along the row, so one knob can morph the tone (Vital source, synth_parameters.cpp: "Wave Frame").
- It has three oscillators and a **Sample** slot (Vital source, synth_constants.h and synth_parameters.cpp); on this page the Sample slot holds noise (a guess).
- Its filter has eight **models** (Analog, Dirty, Ladder, Digital, Diode, Formant, Comb, Phaser) and **styles** such as 12 dB and 24 dB (Vital source, synth_strings.h). This page plays only three of them, with its own filters.
- You **modulate** a knob by dragging an envelope or LFO onto it (vital.audio: "drag and drop").
- This page's Vital is a **beginner panel**: three oscillators on one basic-shapes table (sine, triangle, square, saw), one filter, two envelopes, one LFO, three effects. The real plug-in has far more.

## Guided tour

Each step loads a starting patch made on this page (not one of Vital's own presets) and plays it. After each step, turn one knob on the panel and listen again.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-first"><p><b>Make a first sound.</b> Oscillator 1 is on, <b>Wave frame</b> at 256 (the saw end of the table), the filter open. Listen: a bright, buzzy tone. Now drag <b>Wave frame</b> down to 0: the sound turns into a soft sine.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-first" data-set="{&quot;cut&quot;:70,&quot;res&quot;:45}"><p><b>Shape it with the filter.</b> The same sound with <b>Cutoff</b> down to 70 semitones and <b>Resonance</b> at 45 %. Listen: darker, with a ring on top. Cutoff takes away high harmonics; resonance boosts the ones near the cutoff.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-morph"><p><b>Shape it with the wavetable.</b> <b>Env 2 → wave frame</b> at 256: on every note envelope 2 moves the wave from sine towards saw. Listen: the tone brightens along each note with no filter sweep. This is what a wavetable synth does best.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-bass"><p><b>A bass.</b> A saw an octave down with a sine two octaves down under it, a <b>24dB Ladder</b> filter nearly closed, <b>Env 2 → cutoff</b> opening it on each note, <b>Polyphony 1</b> and a little <b>portamento</b>. Listen for the low weight and the "wow" at each note's start.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-pad"><p><b>A pad.</b> Two oscillators a few cents apart (<b>Tune</b> -8 and +8), between triangle and square, a slow <b>attack</b> and <b>release</b> on envelope 1, <b>LFO 1 → wave frame</b> moving slowly, chorus and reverb. Listen: chords that swell in and shimmer.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-lead"><p><b>A lead.</b> Saw plus a brighter wave an octave up, <b>Unison voices</b> 4, the LFO giving vibrato, portamento and a delay. Play it from the keys and hold a note to hear the vibrato.</p></div>
```

## What the real Vital can do that this page can't

The panel above is a **beginner** Vital: the knobs that are not dimmed are the ones this page plays (**Show ▾ → Only working controls** hides the rest). Counts for the real plug-in are from its source code (synth_constants.h and synth_parameters.cpp, read 2026-11-27).

| | The real Vital | This page |
|---|---|---|
| **Modulation** | Drag any of 6 envelopes, 8 LFOs, 4 random LFOs, 4 macros, velocity or the wheels onto **any** knob; up to 64 connections, each with its own amount, and (per the source, read in part) bipolar, stereo, curve and bypass settings | **No assigning.** Five fixed routes only: Env 2 → cutoff, Env 2 → wave frame, LFO 1 → pitch, LFO 1 → cutoff, LFO 1 → wave frame. Env 1 always shapes the loudness |
| **Wavetables** | Any wavetable: load your own (.wav, .flac, .vitaltable); 257 frames per table | One table (sine → triangle → square → saw), the frame knob only |
| **Oscillators** | 3 oscillators, each with spectral morph, distortion (warp), unison up to 16 with stack styles, stereo spread, phase and routing to either filter, both, the effects or straight out | 3 oscillators: on, frame, transpose, tune, level; unison up to 8; all go into the one filter |
| **Sampler** | Plays a .wav or .flac sample, looped or keytracked | Noise only (a stand-in) |
| **Filters** | 2 filters + a filter effect; 8 models (Analog, Dirty, Ladder, Digital, Diode, Formant, Comb, Phase) and their styles; formant and comb settings; filter-to-filter routing | 1 filter, 3 models, this site's own filter code |
| **Envelopes** | 6, each with delay, hold and curved attack / decay / release | 2 plain ADSRs |
| **LFOs** | 8 LFOs (shapes saved as .vitallfo files), tempo sync, fade-in, delay, smoothing, stereo, keytrack; plus 4 random LFOs | 1 LFO, 4 fixed shapes, free rate |
| **Macros** | 4 macro knobs, each assignable | None |
| **Effects** | 9: chorus, multiband compressor, delay, distortion, 3-band EQ, filter, flanger, phaser, reverb, in **any order**, each fully adjustable | 3: chorus, delay, reverb, mix only, fixed order |
| **Voices** | Up to 32 notes, voice priority, legato, portamento slope / force / scale, pitch bend up to 48 semitones, MPE, 4 oversampling settings, stereo routing | Up to 16 notes, glide time only |
| **The sound** | Vital's own code | This site's own engine with Vital's names and ranges: close, not the same |

## Get the real Vital (free)

1. Go to **vital.audio**, make an account and download Vital (the README: "Create an account and download Vital at vital.audio"). Choose the free *Basic* version.
2. Install it. vital.audio lists Windows 10 and higher, macOS 10.15 and higher, and Ubuntu Linux 18.04 and above; the plug-in formats it installs are listed on its download page (not checked here).
3. Open your DAW (for example GarageBand, Logic, Ableton Live or Reaper), make a new instrument track and choose **Vital** as its instrument. Play a key: you should hear its starting sound.
4. If you hear nothing, check that the track is armed or selected and that the DAW's audio output is your speakers or headphones.

## Copy the patch across

Make a sound on the panel above (a tour step, then your own changes). Then:

1. Press **Show the settings to copy** below. Each row is one control of the panel above, as it is now. **This page** is the number on this site's panel; **In the plug-in** is what the real plug-in should show for it, where this page knows how to work that out (the conversion laws are this page's reading of the plug-in's source or manual and are unverified, so trust your ears more than the numbers).
2. In Vital, on each oscillator: switch it on, choose a basic-shapes wavetable (Vital's factory *Basic Shapes*, name unverified), then set **Wave Frame**, **Transpose**, **Tune** and **Level**.
3. Switch **Filter 1** on (it starts off: its *on* switch defaults to off in Vital's source), then set **Model**, **Style**, **Blend**, **Cutoff**, **Resonance**, **Drive** and **Key Track**. Send the oscillators you use into Filter 1.
4. Set **Envelope 1** (in Vital it shapes the loudness: our reading, unverified) and **Envelope 2**. Drag Envelope 2 onto the **Cutoff** knob, then set how far it moves it; do the same for the wave frame if this page's patch uses it.
5. Set **LFO 1**'s shape and frequency, and drag it onto pitch, cutoff or wave frame as in the table.
6. Turn on **Chorus**, **Delay** and **Reverb** in Vital's effects if the table has them, and set their mix.
7. Play the same notes on both. They will not sound the same: this page's oscillators, filters and effects are its own, not Vital's code. Change the plug-in until it sounds right to you, then **save the preset**.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-copy" data-id="vital"></div>
```

## Check yourself

Click an answer. You will see at once if it is right. Nothing is saved or sent.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>What does the Wave frame knob do?</b></p><ul><li>Picks a place in the wavetable, changing the wave</li><li>Changes the volume</li><li>Adds echo</li><li>Picks the filter model</li></ul><p class="ik-why">A wavetable is a row of waves; Wave Frame picks one (synth_parameters.cpp).</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>How do you make an LFO move a knob in Vital?</b></p><ul><li>Drag the LFO onto the knob</li><li>Type a code</li><li>Plug in a cable</li><li>It cannot</li></ul><p class="ik-why">vital.audio: drag and drop modulation.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>Which part takes away high harmonics?</b></p><ul><li>The filter (Cutoff)</li><li>The LFO</li><li>The delay</li><li>Polyphony</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Step 2.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>Is there a free version of Vital?</b></p><ul><li>Yes, Basic</li><li>No, it is only sold</li><li>Only on phones</li><li>Only as hardware</li></ul><p class="ik-why">The README speaks of "the free version of Vital"; vital.audio lists Basic.</p></div>
```
